baseline_models.focus_anchor: نَافَقُوا ... لِإِخْوَانِهِمْ ... لَئِنْ أُخْرِجْتُمْ لَنَخْرُجَنَّ مَعَكُمْ ... لَنَنْصُرَنَّكُمْ ... لَكَاذِبُونَ
baseline_models.mechanism: The speakers package two costly tests, co-departure and armed aid, as the conduct required by a binding brother-relation. Yet the focus root for hypocrisy supplies a public entrance with a concealed exit, so the pledge itself has a double architecture: visible solidarity and preserved private escape. The final lie-label exposes the claimed bond as staged rather than operative.

activation_trace.role: Displaying one entrance while hiding another supplies the pledge's split architecture and the speakers' retained escape route.
The fastening bond makes 'brothers' a claim of binding attachment rather than a casual label.
The paired expulsion and departure forms make bodily co-exit the first practical test of the bond.
Aid that makes another prevail supplies the second practical test, support under attack.
Contrariety to truth adjudicates both promised tests as a false performance of attachment.

changed_reading.before: Hypocrites make two false promises to political allies.
changed_reading.after: The verse displays a counterfeit alliance contract whose public kinship and matched commitments conceal a private exit from every cost.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: يَقُولُونَ ... لَنَخْرُجَنَّ ... لَا نُطِيعُ ... أَحَدًا أَبَدًا ... لَنَنْصُرَنَّكُمْ وَاللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ
baseline_models.mechanism: The speakers try to manufacture credibility by accumulating emphatic futures, universal negation, and unlimited duration. Their saying therefore acts as self-produced evidence. God's knowledge-backed testimony interrupts that verbal inflation and makes witnessed truth, rather than pledge volume, the governing evidentiary regime.

activation_trace.role: Voiced speech supplies the medium through which the speakers attempt to make future loyalty publicly credible.
Indefinite 'anyone' under negation universalizes the claimed refusal of outside command.
Unbounded duration extends the claimed loyalty beyond any foreseeable test.
Knowledge-backed declaration supplies an external verdict able to overrule the speakers' self-attestation.
The truth/falsehood boundary converts emphatic wording from proof of loyalty into evidence of overperformed deception.

changed_reading.before: The verse reports a lie and then corrects it.
changed_reading.after: The verse stages a contest between two kinds of evidence: self-amplifying political speech and divine testimony grounded in knowledge.

baseline_models.mechanism: The middle promise exceeds companionship: it offers permanent noncompliance with every outside commander in the recipients' matter. Brotherhood is thereby presented as a rival command hierarchy, with factional attachment claiming priority over any competing authority; the divine witness at the close places that absolute political claim under a higher allegiance.

activation_trace.role: Kinship-like affiliation supplies the social unit to which privileged loyalty is promised.
Obedient submission supplies the command relation that the speakers claim they will categorically refuse elsewhere.
Negative indefiniteness expands the refusal across every possible outside claimant.
Perpetuity turns a situational assurance into a claim of enduring command priority.
The divine object of worship supplies the ultimate allegiance horizon against which the factional absolute is judged.

changed_reading.before: The speakers reassure their allies that they will ignore pressure from others.
changed_reading.after: They offer the allies a counter-sovereignty: an indefinite exemption from every competing command, secured only by deceptive speech.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next ayah reruns the focus pledge as an execution trace. It denies co-departure, denies aid under attack, and then grants the hypothetical aid only to drive it into flight and final non-aid. The focus verdict 'liars' is thus not a generic character judgment; it is the result of testing each promised branch in sequence.

activation_trace.role: The focus verdict establishes the proposition that the following replay tests against action.
Repeated outward movement directly reopens and then negates the first promised test, co-departure.
Mutual combat reinstates the focus condition under which aid had been guaranteed.
The three aid forms negate aid, hypothetically concede it, and end in lack of aid, exhausting the promise's possible outcomes.
Turning away reverses the promised movement 'with you' into abandonment.
Showing the back gives the reversal a visible bodily endpoint: pledged supporters become fugitives.

structural_cues: 59:12 repeats the focus's conditional order, departure before combat-aid, and negates each result before adding a flight outcome.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies exact lexical replay, negations, and the added turning of backs; I infer that the replay functions as a clause-by-clause audit of the pledge. A live alternative is that 59:12 is simply prediction, without emphasis on an evidentiary test structure.

changed_reading.before: God labels the speakers liars without displaying the basis inside the focus ayah.
changed_reading.after: The lie is an executable contract that immediately fails every branch, including the strongest hypothetical rescue of its aid clause.

context_deltas.mechanism: The three preceding ayat supply an enacted grammar of affiliation: expelled people bear real loss and actively aid; hosts prefer others over themselves; later believers call predecessors brothers while asking that concealed rancor be removed. Against that sequence, the focus speakers copy the vocabulary of departure, aid, saying, and brotherhood but replace incurred cost and cleansed interiors with emphatic future talk. Their 'brothers' is therefore a counterfeit of the community just modeled.

activation_trace.role: The mismatch between displayed affiliation and concealed departure supplies the counterfeit mechanism.
Actual forced departure supplies an already-incurred cost, contrasting with the focus's merely promised co-departure.
Active aid supplies realized support rather than a future assurance contingent on someone else's danger.
Truth as fulfilled promise and action joins the truth-label to costly conduct.
Choosing another over oneself supplies the cost-bearing direction missing from the hypocrites' assurances.
Another voiced saying creates a controlled comparison between two forms of community speech.
Brotherhood here reaches absent predecessors through prayer, supplying a nontransactional foil to the focus affiliation.
Hidden rancor in the chest makes interior cleansing part of genuine brotherhood, opposite the concealed exit of hypocrisy.

structural_cues: 59:8-10 moves from dispossession and aid, to self-preference, to brother-directed prayer; 59:11 follows with the same social vocabulary in future emphatics.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacency, repeated roots, realized costs, and opposed truth labels; I infer a deliberate counterfeit relation between the two communities' vocabularies. The alternative is that 59:8-10 only supplies general moral contrast, not a term-by-term template for 59:11.

changed_reading.after: 'Their brothers' is an appropriated covenant word: the speakers mimic the language of costly, inwardly cleansed solidarity while withholding its actions.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier command sequence establishes a legitimate circuit: receive what the Messenger gives, stop where he forbids, and guard oneself before God. The focus promise to obey no one concerning the allies forever can therefore be heard not only as resistance to pressure but as a pledge to disable that corrective circuit. The speakers sell solidarity by promising exemption from accountable command.

activation_trace.role: Obedient submission is the relation categorically denied in the allies' matter.
Universal scope makes the refusal capable of including the legitimate commander established by context.
Unlimited duration removes the refusal from a single tactical dispute and makes it a standing exemption.
The Messenger and message supply the authorized human node in the command circuit.
Taking and receiving supplies the positive mode of compliant response.
Prohibition and cessation supply the corrective command that factional loyalty threatens to block.
Placing oneself under protection before God restores accountability beyond the allies' promised exemption.

structural_cues: 59:7 pairs an imperative to take with an imperative to desist; 59:11 answers with an absolute first-person refusal to obey anyone 'concerning you.'
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an earlier Messenger-centered command structure and the focus's universal refusal; I infer that the refusal can reach that legitimate structure. The live alternative is narrower: 'anyone' may denote only political pressure from unnamed third parties, not the Messenger specifically.

changed_reading.before: The non-obedience clause is a generic promise of steadfast loyalty.
changed_reading.after: The clause markets an unaccountable enclave in which loyalty to the allies overrides the surah's receive-and-desist command structure.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus repeatedly says 'with you' and invokes brotherhood, verbally compressing two parties into one front. Later context locates their courage inside fortified settlements and behind walls, while twice invoking togetherness only to expose scattered hearts. Fear and enclosure, not an integrated bond, manufacture their apparent coalition; emphatic promises compensate for internal spatial separation.

activation_trace.role: A fastening social bond supplies the unity claimed by the speakers.
Joint aid supplies the promised public expression of that unity.
Contracting fear supplies the inward pressure organizing the coalition's behavior.
Mutual combat supplies the practical arena in which promised togetherness should become visible.
Gathering what is separate supplies the repeated appearance of a unified body.
Protection inside an enclosing fort makes cohesion dependent on defensive containment.
The raised wall gives the coalition's separating and protective geometry a concrete boundary.
The heart relocates the decisive measure of union from public grouping to inward organization.
Dispersion directly undoes the apparent gathering and exposes the coalition as internally plural.

structural_cues: 59:14 repeats 'all together' around fortified places and walls, then pivots from apparent gathering to 'their hearts are scattered.'
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies fear, combat, enclosures, repeated gathering, and scattered hearts; I infer that the focus's emphatic 'with you' language is compensatory verbal binding. The alternative is a narrower tactical description of combat readiness with no claim about why the promises are rhetorically excessive.

changed_reading.before: The speakers claim that two allied groups will act as one.
changed_reading.after: Their unity is a verbal and architectural enclosure around scattered interiors; 'with you' is strongest exactly where shared courage is absent.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later similitude supplies a speech-act sequence: an instigator speaks, the hearer incurs the dangerous act, and the instigator then declares separation while invoking fear of God. Read through that sequence, the focus assurances are not merely inaccurate forecasts; they are inducements that transfer exposure to the recipients while the speakers preserve a later disavowal route.

activation_trace.role: A displayed entrance and concealed exit supplies the instigator's ability to solicit action while retaining separation.
A represented similitude explicitly offers the later sequence as a reusable explanatory pattern.
Distance and severance supply the endpoint hidden behind the instigator's initial proximity.
Two voiced sayings bracket the other's action, first inducing and then redefining the relation.
The commanded and completed rejection supplies the costly act borne by the hearer between the two speeches.
Declared separation supplies the explicit abandonment that the focus promise conceals.
Anticipated harm supplies the self-protective rationale asserted only after the other party has acted.

structural_cues: 59:16 places compliance between two sayings: command first, then 'I am quit of you' after the commanded act occurs.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an explicit similitude and the inducement-action-disavowal order; I infer an asymmetric transfer of risk back into 59:11. A live alternative is betrayal without calculated prior intent: the speakers may fail from fear rather than have designed the exit from the outset.

changed_reading.before: The hypocrites lie about what they themselves will do later.
changed_reading.after: Their promises function as risk-transfer speech: they encourage the recipients to hold out while reserving the right to separate once danger becomes real.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus juxtaposes hypocrisy's displayed/hidden split with God's testimony. The closing divine names then pair knowledge with the hidden and the witnessed and add supervisory testimony-care. God's verdict therefore crosses the exact boundary on which the deception depends: public utterance and concealed disposition are simultaneously present to the witness.

activation_trace.role: The visible entrance and hidden exit establish the epistemic split the speakers rely upon.
Knowledge-backed testimony supplies the focus verdict that penetrates the split.
Disclosure to the knower supplies the epistemic ground of the testimony rather than mere inference from appearances.
What is screened from eyes supplies the concealed intention and escape path inaccessible to ordinary observers.
The present and witnessed domain supplies the audible promises and public affiliation paired with the hidden.
Testimony joined to watchful care extends the verdict into ongoing supervision of whether speech becomes action.

structural_cues: 59:22 directly coordinates 'the hidden and the witnessed'; 59:23 follows with the divine name associated in the packet with testimony and care.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the hidden/witnessed pair and supervisory testimony after the focus's divine witness; I infer backward illumination of how that witness knows the lie. The alternative is that the closing names are a general doxological conclusion rather than a specific gloss on 59:11.

changed_reading.before: God predicts that the emphatic promises will prove false.
changed_reading.after: God's testimony is already adequate because it simultaneously apprehends the public pledge and the concealed disposition that will abandon it.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier expulsion scene shows confidence placed in enclosing fortresses: imagined protection fails under fear and turns into the occupants' own demolition. The focus then answers the prospect of expulsion with maximal verbal enclosure, surrounding the recipients with 'with you,' 'no one,' 'ever,' and doubled emphatic futures. The alliance speech can be read as a rhetorical fortress reproducing the failed security logic of the material one.

activation_trace.role: Voiced saying supplies the material from which the substitute enclosure is built.
Unlimited duration rhetorically closes the promise against every future breach.
Actual and expected outward movement supplies the material crisis that both fortress and promise attempt to prevent or accompany.
Uncertain imagining supplies the mistaken confidence projected onto defensive means.
Protective strength that bars access supplies the expected function of the physical fortress.
Preservation inside an enclosing fort supplies the spatial model transferred to emphatic language.
Fear supplies the force that bypasses the enclosure and collapses confidence from within.
Ruin of built habitation supplies the endpoint of security that destroys itself from inside.

structural_cues: 59:2 narrates actual expulsion despite trusted fortresses; 59:11 responds to expulsion with enclosing absolutes and emphatic future clauses.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies failed physical enclosure and later maximal verbal assurance around the same expulsion root; I supply the cross-domain arrow from fortress to rhetoric. The live alternative is that the shared security function is incidental and no material analogy is intended.

changed_reading.before: The speakers offer emotional reassurance after a military loss.
changed_reading.after: Their emphatic pledge is a verbal fortification: another imagined barrier against expulsion whose hidden internal failure repeats the walls' collapse.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it transfers a physical tunnel image to a political utterance. It remains anchored in the focus's نفاق, the packet's branch of a through-passage with an exit, the branch of a displayed entrance with a hidden exit, and the doubled خروج. Downstream prose should present it as a material analogy for the pledge's design, not as a lexical translation of نَافَقُوا.

activation_trace.role: A through-passage with an outlet supplies the speech's image as a route that can be entered and escaped.
The public door and concealed exit assign different routes to the audience and the speakers.
Negotiation concerning an affair makes the utterance the constructed passage through which alliance is proposed.
Paired outward movement anchors the tunnel analogy in the verse's own repeated exit language.

changed_reading.before: The promise verbally joins the speakers to the recipients' path.
changed_reading.after: The promise behaves like a two-exit passage: it guides the recipients toward reliance while preserving a concealed route out for its makers.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the packet's livestock image of milk expected to continue but then ceasing. It remains anchored by the direct collision between أَبَدًا, the lie root, and 59:12's repeated denial of aid. Downstream prose should qualify it as a temporal durability analogy, never as the lexical meaning of كَاذِبُونَ in this ayah.

activation_trace.role: Perpetual duration supplies the promise's explicit claim never to run out.
A supply thought durable but then gone supplies a concrete image for the pledge's failed continuity.
Repeated aid language ending in non-aid supplies the observed cessation of what was advertised as dependable support.

changed_reading.before: The word 'ever' is ordinary rhetorical exaggeration inside a lie.
changed_reading.after: The lie's special defect is failed duration: it advertises an inexhaustible supply of loyalty that disappears at the first draw on it.

strongest_changes: 59:12 turns the divine lie-verdict into a clause-by-clause execution test that fails departure, aid, and even the hypothetical rescue case.
59:8-10 makes the focus's brother-language a counterfeit of solidarity already realized through loss, aid, self-preference, prayer, and inward cleansing.
59:16 changes the promises from inaccurate prediction into possible inducement and asymmetric risk transfer followed by disavowal.
59:13-14 relocates the coalition's unity from its emphatic 'with you' speech to fear, forts, walls, and scattered hearts.
59:22-23 explains the adequacy of God's witness as knowledge spanning both the public pledge and its hidden exit.
summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah builds an unusually total alliance in speech: paired conditional futures, co-movement, aid, universal refusal, and perpetual duration. The packet's branch images reveal that this verbal enclosure is organized around a concealed exit, while neighboring ayat repeatedly test it against costly action, legitimate command, interior cohesion, and knowledge of the hidden.
remaining_uncertainties: The earlier Messenger-centered command structure makes a specific referent for 'anyone' plausible, but the focus construction itself leaves that referent indefinite.
The verbal-fortress and failed-durability readings are cross-domain analogies and should not displace the direct social and evidentiary readings.
The inducement-disavowal sequence supports asymmetric risk transfer, but it does not by itself prove that the speakers consciously planned betrayal before making the promise.
